confidence_explanation: High confidence assigned based on converging multi-source empirical evidence: bootstrap rank-1 frequency is 100.0% with mean rank 1.00; statistically significant Holm-adjusted pairwise superiority over all 6 evaluated competitors with zero pairwise defeats; confirmed non-dominated Pareto status across intrinsic and operational criteria. This label reflects structural evidence consensus across resampling and conditions, not a mathematical probability.
statistical_evidence: Bootstrap 95% Confidence Interval for Top-1 Mean: [0.5281, 0.6342]
Holm-Adjusted Wilcoxon Pairwise Comparisons: 6 significant wins, 0 defeats
Omnibus Friedman test confirms statistically significant model separation across matched benchmark conditions (p < 1e-20)
robustness_evidence: Representation Stability: Mean rank 1.2 across JSON, Key-Value, Mixed, Narrative, Template formats (Std: 0.45)
Subset Stability: Mean rank 1.0 across balanced, high, medium, low knowledge subsets and random baseline (Std: 0.0)

mecs_evidence: Baseline MECS Score: 87.4000 (Rank 1 in baseline scenario)
MECS Scenario Wins: 3 wins across 4 weight scenarios (Win frequency: 0.75)

MECS Sensitivity Trade-off: ModernBERT leads performance-oriented and baseline scenarios; general BERT leads vocabulary/domain-heavy scenarios, exposing an explicit capability versus tokenization trade-off.

tradeoffs.observation: Higher subword fragmentation rate (62.99%) relative to specialized WordPiece tokenizers (e.g. BERT at 26.57%).
tradeoffs.implication: Treated as a tokenizer operational limitation to monitor during pretraining, not as an automatic decision rejection trigger.

tradeoffs.observation: Parameter count of 149.0M and latency of 28.74ms, compared to 110M parameter architectures (e.g. BERT-base at 19.51ms).
tradeoffs.implication: Incurs higher inference and training overhead; acceptable given substantial intrinsic language modeling superiority.

relative_advantages: higher rare maritime token accuracy (80.70% vs 77.34%)

limitations: Benchmark evidence supports the selected model as the preferred pretrained initialization for subsequent DAPT, but does NOT prove downstream task optimality prior to empirical adaptation.
Empirical downstream validation on fine-tuned classification, extraction, and incident summarization tasks remains required in subsequent DAPT stages.
MECS is an operational composite score used for supporting sensitivity analysis; it is not a direct mathematical ground truth of maritime understanding.
